open_points.subject: A18
open_points.text:
Third, whatever the second step did, it deletes every kept
backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before the instant this step starts,
one cutoff for the whole step — a backup made exactly 30 × 24 hours before
it is kept.

after a run whose deletions succeeded: no backup older than 30 × 24 hours and no
  backup that failed its check exists
open_points.question: Is “older than 30 × 24 hours” in the formal invariant measured against the third step's fixed starting cutoff, or against the later instant when the run finishes?
options: Measure age against the one cutoff read when the third step starts, so a backup that crosses 720 hours while deletion runs remains kept.
Measure age when the run finishes, requiring deletion of a backup that crossed 720 hours during the step.
open_points.default_guess: Rewrite the invariant to refer explicitly to the third step's fixed cutoff.

witness.initial: At the third step's clock reading, a kept backup is 719 hours, 59 minutes and 59 seconds old; deleting other files then takes two seconds.
events: Registry reads the one cutoff at the start of the third step.
The backup is not earlier than that cutoff.
The run finishes after the backup has become more than 720 hours old.
outcomes: The normative rule keeps the backup because it was not earlier than the fixed cutoff.
Reading the formal invariant at run completion requires that no now-older backup remain.
witness.observer: The owner listing the kept backups after the run

open_points.subject: A18
open_points.text:
The cutoff and
each record's UTC instant (L16) are compared as instants at the full
precision each holds, neither rounded nor truncated; a backup whose
instant is earlier than the cutoff is deleted.
open_points.question: What exact representation and precision do backup-record instants and the clock-derived cutoff use, including whether precision is uniform when an instant is recorded?
options: Store and compare every instant at one specified precision, such as an aware UTC datetime with microseconds.
Permit records and clock readings to have different precisions, treating every stored value as the exact instant denoted by its own representation.
Preserve the source clock's varying precision in each record and define an explicit common-precision comparison rule.
open_points.default_guess: Use timezone-aware UTC datetimes with microsecond precision for both recorded instants and cutoff readings.

witness.initial: A backup is actually made at 03:00:00.750 UTC; thirty days later the third step's cutoff is 03:00:00.500 UTC.
events: One implementation records the backup instant with microseconds.
Another implementation's permitted record representation stores only whole seconds.
The retention step compares the record with its cutoff without changing the precision each stored value holds.
outcomes: The microsecond record is later than the cutoff and the backup is kept.
The whole-second record denotes 03:00:00 UTC, is earlier than the cutoff and the backup is deleted.
witness.observer: The owner viewing the newest kept backup

open_points.subject: A18
open_points.text:
7. With the step's cutoff fixed at its start, a kept backup made exactly
   30 × 24 hours before it is kept and one made a second earlier is deleted.
open_points.question: What Required tests item demonstrates the new invariant that comparison uses the full precision of both instants without rounding or truncation at a coarser boundary?
options: Add a sub-second boundary case on opposite sides of the cutoff and assert the corresponding keep and delete outcomes.
State that all persisted and clock instants have exactly one fixed precision, then test the smallest representable unit around the cutoff.
Remove the full-precision requirement and define comparison at whole-second precision, matching the existing test.
open_points.default_guess: Specify one uniform instant precision and add cases one smallest representable unit before, equal to, and after the cutoff.
